reason: The deck has a named caster slot, and the ball caster fits it.
expectation: The caster should fit into the deck and help support the rover.

effect: The caster is installed, and the deck accepts the drive and electrical modules in any order. The two driven wheels will steer by running at different speeds.
reaction: The explanation of turning without a steering axle is interesting.
reason: The rubber wheels and matched gearmotors appear to be the parts needed for the wheel drives.
expectation: The wheels should attach to the gearmotors to make the rover’s drives.

effect: The wheels and gearmotors are now wheel drives; the gearboxes trade speed for greater turning force.
reaction: The speed-and-force tradeoff is useful to understand.
reason: The deck has a named slot for the assembled wheel drives.
expectation: The wheel drives should fit into the deck.

effect: The wheel drives are installed alongside the caster; the electrical modules still need fitting.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The rover deck has a named battery slot, so the battery pack is a clear fit.
expectation: The battery pack should slot into the deck, with its connector parked and the switch kept off.

effect: The battery pack is installed; the switch harness and receiver remain to be fitted.
reason: The deck has a named switch harness slot.
expectation: The switch harness should slot into the deck, with the switch kept off.

effect: The switch harness is installed; the receiver still needs fitting.
reason: The receiver and motor driver match the deck’s remaining named receiver slot.
expectation: The receiver and motor driver should slot into the deck.

effect: The receiver and motor driver are installed, filling the deck’s named slots.
reason: The gear guards appear to belong over the installed wheel drives.
expectation: The guards should cover the rover’s drive gears.

alternatives.reason: The remote also needs power before testing.

effect: The rover is wired and guarded, with its wheels clear for a remote test.
reaction: The test stops are a sensible way to check the drives before letting the rover move.
reason: The remote needs its batteries before it can control the rover.
expectation: The batteries should power the remote for testing.

effect: The remote now has batteries and is ready to test the guarded rover.
reason: The guarded rover is ready for the remote, with its wheels clear on the test stops.
expectation: The remote should let me test whether the rover’s wheels respond independently.

effect: The remote test confirmed that the wheel drives respond, and the chapter’s goal is complete. Radio carries instructions while the batteries supply energy.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the assembled rover respond, though the test was brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the wheel drives was worthwhile because the gearbox explanation showed how slower rotation gives more turning force.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the battery, switch and receiver was straightforward but a little repetitive.

surprise.text: The rover can turn by running its two driven wheels at different speeds, without a steering axle.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the named slots made the module fittings clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the tested rover earns a pen and draws an invitation, especially if that adds another mechanism to explore.
